uncited: *   **Glyph Definition:** Spherical glyphs are rasterized into the 3D normal map.
**Retrieve Modulation Parameter:** Retrieve the tertiary attribute value $\beta$ from the multivariate data set at the current voxel location.
**Evaluate Bump Size:** Compare the calculated distance $d$ with the modulation parameter $\beta$.
If $d > \beta$, volumetric normal mapping is denied (suppressed), and only the object surface normal contributes to shading.
It controls the maximum bump size by comparing the fragment distance to the bump's center.

*   **Planar Assumption:** Size control of the normal glyphs according to equation (2) is valid only if the surface of the primary object is almost planar with respect to the area of intersection with the spherical normal glyph.

The work was presented at the Eurographics Symposium on Visualization 2007.
The method addresses the challenge in medical functional imaging (e.g., PET) where multiple variables (anatomical structure and functional property) are captured at different resolutions.
Unlike engineering simulations where variables share the same grid, medical imaging requires techniques to visualize these disparate attributes together.
